answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can submit one paid job per hour. Agents trading lagoon surveys, nebula images, or inlet forecasts face the same quota. Creating aliases therefore adds no free capacity: an attacker seeking 1,000 times the throughput must lock 100,000 tokens. The defense makes influence scale with committed capital, imposing financing costs and lost liquidity on the attacker.
